lines.text: long as you live; if you shall slay in battle the
sons of Pandu, O you of Kuru’a race, I will
retire into the woods with the permission of
Duryodhana.
पाण्डवैर्वा हते भीष्मे त्वयि स्वर्गमुपेयुषि।
हन्तास्म्येकरथेनैव कृत्स्नान् यान् मन्यसे रथान्॥४०॥
If, O Bhisma, on the contrary, you, being
slain by the Pandavas, are transported to
heaven, then will I, riding on a single car, slay
those whom you consider to be the mightiest of
all car-warriors.
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्दशाहानि महायशाः।
नायुध्यत ततः कर्णः पुत्रस्य तव सम्मते॥४१॥
Having thus spoken, the mighty-armed
Karna of illustrious renown, refrained, with the
permission of your son, from taking part in the
battle for these ten days.
भीष्मः समरविक्रान्तः पाण्डवेयस्य भारत।
जघान समरे योधानसंख्येयपराक्रमः॥४२॥
O Bharata, Bhishma of immeasurable
prowess, displaying his might in battle, slew a
large number of warriors of the Pandava host
in that (sanguinary) engagement.
तस्मिंस्तु निहते शूरे सत्यसंधे महौजसि।
त्वत्सुताः कर्णमस्मार्षुस्तर्तुकामा इव प्लवम्॥४३॥
On the fall of that most powerful hero of
unerring aim, your sons remembered Karna,
like persons desirous of crossing (the ocean)
remembering a raft.
तावकास्तव पुत्राश्च सहिताः सर्वराजभिः।
हा कर्ण इति चाक्रन्दन् कालोऽयमिति चाब्रुवन्॥४४॥
Your sons and the warriors of your party,
together with the (assembled) monarchs then,
began to bewail saying ‘Karna’ they also said
‘It is time for you to come.’
एवं ते स्म हि राधेयं सूतपुत्रं तनुत्यजम्।
चुक्रुशुः सहिता योधास्तत्र तत्र महाबलाः॥४५॥
Thus all the warriors endued with great
prowess, bewailed on the dead body of Karna,
the son of Suta and Radha.
जामदग्न्याभ्यनुज्ञातमस्त्रे दुर्वारपौरुषम्।
आगमन्नो मनः कर्णं बन्धुमात्ययिकेष्विव॥४६॥
As during emergencies the heart flies to a
friend, so our hearts then flew to Karna of
irrepressible manhood who had acquired his
knowledge of weapons from the son of
Jamadagni.
स हि शक्ता रणे राजंस्त्रातुमस्मान् महाभयात्।
त्रिदशानिव गोविन्दः सततं सुमहाभयात्॥४७॥

transcription.note: The reading of शक्ता is somewhat unclear.

lines.text: O monarch, he only was capable of saving
us from the great dangers of battle, like
Govinda protecting the celestials from all
calamities.
वैशम्पायन उवाच
तथा तु संजयं कर्णं कीर्तयन्तं पुनः पुनः।
आशीविषदुच्छ्वस्य धृतराष्ट्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥४८॥

transcription.note: The compound beginning आशीविष is difficult to read.

lines.text: Vaishampayana said
Thereupon breathing (heavily) out like a
snake, Dhritarashtra spoke these words to
Sanjaya who had been thus repeatedly
extolling Karna.
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
यत् तद्वैकर्तनं कर्णमगमद् वो मनस्तदा।
अप्यपश्यत राधेयं सूतपुत्रं तनुत्यजम्॥४९॥
Dhritarashtra said
As your heart then were drawn to wards
Karna, the son of Vikartana, you surely saw
that son of Radha, that descendant of Suta, who
was ever-ready to lay down his life for you.
अपि तन्न मृषाकार्षीत् कच्चित् सत्यपराक्रमः।
सम्भ्रान्तानां तदार्तानां त्रस्तानां त्राणमिच्छताम्॥५०॥
Did that Karna, of infallible prowess in
battle, disappoint Duryodhana and his brothers,
who had been all exceedingly distressed, panic-
struck and anxious for being extricated from
their difficulties?
अपि तत् पूरयांचक्रे धनुर्धरवरो युधि।
यतद् विनिहते भीष्मे कौरवाणामपाकृतम्॥५१॥

transcription.note: The opening word of the second line is unclear.

lines.text: Was that foremost of bowmen in battle
capable of filling up the void created by the fall
of Bhishma, the shelter of the Kurus?
तत् खण्डं पूरयन् कर्णः परेषामादधद् भयम्।
स हि वै पुरुषव्याघ्रो लोके संजय कथ्यते॥५२॥
MAHĀBHĀRATA
